name: legacy_figures_v1
note: Items of the original manuscript's figures (September protocol v1.2 definitions: TSK, VI, SUR, PRE, IMB, OUT16, PRD13, MOD15, VAL02, REP01-19, PROBAST+AI PD/PE, checklist v22 C01-C43) coded for the October studies with the same pipeline.
general_rules: Code only what the report and its supplementary material state; never fill from general knowledge or from what is usual for KNHANES. This is data extraction: record what the report says was done, not whether it was done well (risk of bias is assessed separately later).

status (whether the information is in the report): reported = stated (cite it); not_reported = nothing in the whole input states it; unclear = the report touches it but the exact value cannot be fixed from the text (cite what there is); not_applicable = the object of the item does not exist in this study by design (e.g. no validation dataset exists -> its sample size; outcome not time-to-event -> censoring; no classification at a threshold -> threshold). Not having done a step is NOT not_applicable: if the report states that a step was not done, or cited statements establish it by logic (e.g. 'participants with missing data were excluded' -> no imputation, complete-case; 'inputs were fixed before any model was fitted' -> no data-driven predictor selection), the status is reported with value 'not done (stated)' or 'not done (established: ...)'; if the report is silent about a step the study could have had, it is not_reported. The mere absence of a value is not such a statement: e.g. performance printed without CI or SD -> performance.uncertainty not_reported, not 'reported: none'. Status answers the item's core question (the first sentence of the item, or the part marked 'Core:'). When the core question is answered but a further detail the item asks for is missing (e.g. threshold method stated, threshold number not printed), status is reported and the missing detail is its own value entry with value 'not_reported'. When only a related fact is given but not what the core question asks (e.g. missing data mentioned, no amount), status is not_reported (or unclear) and the related fact goes in the rationale. For validation items: if any validation or test data exist (split sample, cross-validation, bootstrap, external), items about that validation are not not_applicable; e.g. a random split of the same data has no geographic or temporal separation -> reported 'none (random split of the same data)'. not_applicable only when the study has no validation or test data at all; then all validation items are not_applicable except validation.type, which is reported 'no validation (no validation or test data)' (kind judged) so that studies without validation can be counted. Partly missing values never change an answered item to not_reported: e.g. events printed by sex and the overall total not printed -> status reported, the sex-specific values printed and the total, if given, kind derived.

inconsistency (separate from status): none = no contradiction found; present = two places in the report give contradictory information about the same fact, object and condition (e.g. different CIs for the same model and dataset in a table and a figure; different names for the same split); uncertain = possibly contradictory but the places may refer to different objects. Notation (> vs >=) and rounding are not inconsistencies. Describe it in inconsistency_note (both places with IDs), else ''. An inconsistency never changes the status: printed values that disagree are still reported. Scope: the coded report is the included version. Text that the input itself marks as another version or as submission-system material (e.g. an 'Original Manuscript' block with an earlier abstract in a preprint server PDF, an earlier preprint version, cover letters, reviewer reports) is not part of it: do not code from it when the main text gives the fact, and differences between it and the main text are not inconsistencies (inconsistency none; mention it in the rationale). A count of predictors and a count of coefficients or encoded columns (dummy levels, design-matrix columns) are different objects: a difference between them is not an inconsistency (uncertain at most, when the report does not say how predictors were encoded). Record present only when the same variable, model, cohort or split and the same statistic or count, under the same condition, is reported differently (e.g. the same n=3,411 group called validation in the text and Train in a supplementary table). Not inconsistencies: notation or wording differences; using two names (test, validation) for one split when nothing else conflicts; numbers in different units (predictors vs coefficients or design-matrix columns, candidate vs final variables, union of tool inputs vs inputs of each model); different analyses (best model per cohort vs recommended final model; exclusion of some persons and imputation of others). Use uncertain only when the report does not allow telling whether two places refer to the same object.

No unsupported inference: never enter a number, procedure, split or timing that the report does not state. value_kind: printed (copied exactly from text, table cell or figure label - also percentages and counts), derived (you computed it from printed numbers; give the formula in rationale), judged (classification of printed text into the item's categories; one sentence why), approx (read off a figure, prefix ~). Status with derived numbers: if at least one of the item's numbers is printed, status is reported and numbers you add from printed ones (e.g. an overall total summed from printed sex-specific counts) are entries with kind derived; if none of the item's numbers is printed, a derived or approximate number never makes the status reported: status is not_reported (or unclear) and a derived number is given only where the item allows derived values; with no number and nothing to derive it from, not_reported. Never state an absence (e.g. 'no external data', 'no linkage', 'not done', 'whole dataset') unless the report states it; record only what is stated. A phrase like 'all the data were normalised' does not state when the step was done relative to the split: scope not_stated, quote the phrase in the rationale. A figure or table is coded as belonging to a model (e.g. a comparator logistic model) only if its title, legend or text says so. value kind is given per value entry (kind): one item can hold printed and derived numbers side by side (e.g. printed n per sex and a derived total). Linking statements: a step's data scope or procedure may be coded only when the cited statements together name that step and the data it used (e.g. CART predictors taken from the univariable results of Tables 1-2, which are computed on all 672 participants -> that step used the whole dataset). A general statement ('all preprocessing was fitted on the training set') does not fix the scope of a step it does not name (e.g. imputation listed elsewhere), and a table total alone does not show that a step used the whole sample before a split -> not_stated or unclear. kind: printed = text copied as is; when the value is a category of the item assigned from printed text (e.g. '10-fold cross-validation within the training set' -> within_cv_folds; 'nationwide longitudinal survey' -> cohort_study), kind is judged and the printed phrase follows the category.

Unit of extraction: each item says its unit (study, dataset, dataset/split, outcome, model, or evaluation = model x dataset). Give one value entry per unit the report distinguishes and name the unit as the report names it (e.g. 'XGBoost, KNHANES external set'); use unit '' for study-level items. Do not add subgroup entries unless the item's unit includes them. Unit label (canonical): the parts that apply, in this order, separated by ' | ': model | dataset or split | subgroup (e.g. 'CatBoost | KNHANES 2019 test | male'); names as the report gives them; 'all models' (or 'all datasets', 'both sexes') when the same value holds for every unit of that kind, and separate entries only where the values differ. Do not repeat performance rows (performance.estimate) in other items: give the metric names, counts or summary the item asks for.

evidence_ids: every ID you rely on (paragraph P0012, heading S02.01, cell T02-R05-C02, figure element, supplementary paragraph SUPTXT1.P3), copied exactly from the input; at least one for reported and unclear and for inconsistency present/uncertain. IDs not in the input are discarded.

Metrics: name metrics in normalised form followed by the printed name in parentheses when different: AUROC (AUC, ROC-AUC, C-statistic, area under the ROC curve), PR-AUC (AP, average precision, AUPRC), sensitivity (recall, TPR), specificity, PPV (precision), NPV, accuracy, balanced accuracy, F1, MCC, kappa, Brier score, log loss, calibration slope, calibration intercept, R2, RMSE, MAE, net benefit. A metric counts as reported only if a value is printed (table, text, or a value printed in a figure); figure axis labels (e.g. 'True Positive Rate', 'Precision') do not count. Metrics used only for predictor selection or tuning (e.g. LASSO binomial deviance/log loss, CV score used to pick hyperparameters) are not model performance.

Keep apparent (training), internal validation (split sample, cross-validation, bootstrap) and external validation results apart. A held-out split of the same data is never external validation. KNHANES used only for external evaluation counts as external. Cross-validation used only for tuning is recorded under tuning/resampling, not as the validation type of the reported estimates.

Keep apart (each has its own item): predictor availability at intended use; overlap between predictors and the outcome definition; which data each data-dependent step used (leakage-relevant facts); independence of validation data. Record facts in each; do not merge them into one judgement.
Copy printed text exactly; do not translate Korean; quote at most what is needed for the value. For definitions copy the defining phrase, not the whole sentence.

Legacy items: the value is the response code only (e.g. USED, NR, R, P, PY, NI, met, not_met, HEALTH_ANALYSIS, CLS, a topic code), one entry per unit, with no printed detail (put the detail and the printed basis in the rationale); lists of codes are separated by '; '. Exceptions where the value is text: VI06 (named variables, in order, separated by '; '), legacy.age_range, legacy.candidate_predictors (number), legacy.stability_method, legacy.target_population. Status for legacy items: reported whenever a response code is given, including NR, NI, not_met, NOT_USED or UNC (the code carries the judgement); not_applicable only when the item has no object (code NA). PROBAST+AI units: name each unit '<family of the model> | <dataset>' where dataset is development, internal test, cross-validation, bootstrap or external: <name>; code the final or best model of the study and, where the report evaluates several models equally, each of them.

items.legacy.study_category: [unit: study] HEALTH_ANALYSIS = ML used as a tool to analyse a health state or health-related outcome; METHOD_RESEARCH = ML methods themselves developed or improved (develop_or_improve) or existing methods compared as the aim (compare_existing), KNHANES serving as test data. A paper is not method research merely because it compared several algorithms; judge by the author-stated objective. Value: HEALTH_ANALYSIS, or METHOD_RESEARCH: develop_or_improve | compare_existing.
items.legacy.task: [unit: study] (TSK01) Task category based on the actual outcome scale and principal analytic objective Responses: CLS=Categorical-outcome classification; CONT=Continuous-outcome prediction; OTHER=Other analytic task; UNC=Unclear. Classify by the actual analysis, not the algorithm name or authors' terminology. For CONT or OTHER add the kind: continuous_or_ordered | other (e.g. survival, clustering of outputs, generation).
items.legacy.topic: [unit: study] Primary health topic of the main outcome, one of: METABOLIC_ENDOCRINE | MENTAL_HEALTH | CARDIOVASCULAR | MUSCULOSKELETAL | ORAL_HEALTH | RESPIRATORY | KIDNEY_UROLOGIC | CANCER | NUTRITION_DIET | HEALTH_BEHAVIOUR (smoking, alcohol, physical activity, sleep) | OPHTHALMOLOGIC | OTORHINOLARYNGOLOGIC | DERMATOLOGIC_ALLERGIC | INFECTIOUS_IMMUNE | REPRODUCTIVE_WOMENS_HEALTH | AGING_GERIATRIC | GENERAL_HEALTH_MULTIMORBIDITY | OTHER_OR_CROSS_CUTTING. For method research give the topic of the KNHANES outcome used.
items.legacy.year_scope: [unit: study] Survey years analysed: ONE_YEAR (a single survey year) | MULTI_SAME (several years within one KNHANES cycle) | MULTI_CROSS (years from more than one cycle) | UNC. Also give the years as printed.
items.legacy.survey_components: [unit: study] KNHANES components whose variables entered the analysis (outcome or predictors): HEALTH_INTERVIEW | EXAMINATION | LABORATORY | ORAL_HEALTH | NUTRITION (list all that apply; unclear if not stated).
items.legacy.outcome_structure: [unit: study] Structure of the modelled outcome(s): BINARY | MULTIBIN (several separate binary outcomes) | MULTICLASS | MIXED | CONTINUOUS | ORDINAL | OTHER.
items.legacy.outcome_source: [unit: study] Source of the main outcome: questionnaire_or_scale | physical_measurement | laboratory_value | diagnosis_or_history (physician diagnosis or medical history, usually self-reported) | other_or_not_reported.
items.legacy.outcome_timing: [unit: study] current_state_same_survey (outcome measured in the same survey as the predictors) | future_event (outcome after the predictors, e.g. by linkage or follow-up) | timing_unclear.
items.legacy.age_range: [unit: study] (POP03, POP04) Minimum and maximum age of the analysed participants as reported (value 'min: x; max: y'; 'not_reported' for a missing bound).
items.legacy.candidate_predictors: [unit: study] Number of candidate predictors considered before any selection, as reported or countable from a listed set (kind derived when counted).
items.legacy.algorithms_fitted: [unit: study] Algorithm families fitted (all that apply): boosting | random_forest | logistic_regression | decision_tree | svm | neural_network | other (name it).
items.legacy.selected_model: [unit: study] Family of the model the authors designated as final or best: Boosting | Random forest | Logistic regression | Decision tree | SVM | Neural network | Other; 'single_algorithm' if only one algorithm was fitted; 'Not designated' if several were fitted and none was designated.
items.legacy.missing_handling: [unit: study] Missing-data handling: complete_case | single_imputation | multiple_imputation | model_native | other_or_several | not_reported.
items.legacy.target_population: [unit: study] (SUR02) Whom the results are stated to describe: the analysed sample, a stated target population (e.g. Korean adults), or not stated.
items.legacy.VI01: [unit: study] (VI01) Was an explicit model-based variable-importance or explanation method used? Responses: USED; NOT_USED; NR; UNC; NA. USED=an explicit model-based importance/explanation method and its output; NOT_USED=explicit nonuse or an exhaustively described analysis without such output; NR=not reported; UNC=ambiguous evidence; NA=outside classification. Conventional association coefficients alone do not qualify.
items.legacy.VI02: [unit: study] (VI02) Variable-importance or explanation methods Responses: SHAP; MODEL_NATIVE; PERMUTATION; PDP; ALE; ICE; LIME; PERTURBATION_ABLATION; COEFFICIENT_STATISTIC; TREE_RULE; NETWORK_SPECIFIC; NA; OTHER. SHAP; model-native; permutation; PDP; ALE; ICE; LIME; perturbation/ablation; coefficient/statistic; tree/rule; network-specific; other / If OTHER, describe.
items.legacy.VI06: [unit: study] (VI06) Important variable names as reported Responses: . List all variables the authors named as most important, in their order, without a fixed length. A ranking = an ordering or relative importance of variables from a model-based method; regression coefficients alone, or a decision-tree diagram and its split variables alone, do not count.
items.legacy.VI07: [unit: study] (VI07) Standardised domains of important variables Responses: AGE; ADIPOSITY_BODY_SIZE; SEX; BLOOD_PRESSURE; GLYCAEMIA_DIABETES; LIPIDS; KIDNEY_URINE; MENTAL_SUBJECTIVE_HEALTH; SOCIOECONOMIC; DIET; PHYSICAL_ACTIVITY_FUNCTION; SMOKING; ALCOHOL; PAIN_MUSCULOSKELETAL; WORK_CLINICAL_HISTORY; NA; OTHER. age; adiposity/body size; sex; blood pressure; glycaemia/diabetes; lipids; kidney/urine; mental/subjective health; socioeconomic; diet; physical activity/function; smoking; alcohol; pain/musculoskeletal; work/clinical history; other / If OTHER, describe.
items.legacy.VI10: [unit: study] (VI10) Was a reduced model subset defined using importance? Responses: USED; NOT_USED; NR; UNC; NA.
items.legacy.VI11: [unit: study] (VI11) Did ML importance or selection explicitly guide variable choices for subsequent statistical inference? Responses: USED; NOT_USED; NR; UNC; NA.
items.legacy.VI16: [unit: study] (VI16) Was importance stability assessed across resampling, survey cycles, or subgroups? Responses: USED; NOT_USED; NR; UNC; NA. USED=an explicit comparison of importance across resamples, cycles, subgroups or sensitivity analyses; NOT_USED=explicit nonassessment or a documented single ranking only; NR=stability assessment unreported; UNC=ambiguous comparison; NA=no eligible importance output.
items.legacy.stability_method: [unit: study] If VI16 is USED: what varied between the compared rankings (resamples, survey cycles, subgroups, models, sensitivity analyses).
items.legacy.importance_aggregation_weights: [unit: study] Were survey weights used when aggregating participant-level importance (e.g. weighted mean |SHAP|)? USED | NOT_USED | NR | NA (no participant-level importance method such as SHAP or LIME).
items.legacy.SUR04: [unit: study] (SUR04) Were KNHANES sampling weights mentioned? Responses: USED; NOT_USED; NR; UNC; NA. USED=explicit mention of KNHANES survey sampling weights; NOT_USED=explicit statement that sampling weights were not considered; NR=no mention; UNC=weight type unclear; NA=structurally inapplicable. Mention does not establish application in any analysis.
items.legacy.SUR06: [unit: study] (SUR06) Were sampling weights used in model training? Responses: USED; NOT_USED; NR; UNC; NA. USED=KNHANES sampling weights explicitly applied to model fitting; NOT_USED=fitting explicitly unweighted; NR=fitting weights unreported; UNC=weight type or application unclear; NA=no model fitting. Class/loss weights do not qualify.
items.legacy.SUR07: [unit: study] (SUR07) Were sampling weights used in performance evaluation? Responses: USED; NOT_USED; NR; UNC; NA. USED=KNHANES sampling weights explicitly applied to performance metrics; NOT_USED=metrics explicitly unweighted; NR=evaluation weighting unreported; UNC=weight type or application unclear; NA=no performance evaluation.
items.legacy.SUR10: [unit: study] (SUR10) Were strata and clusters accounted for in variance/uncertainty estimation? Responses: USED; NOT_USED; NR; UNC; NA. USED=explicit strata/PSU-aware or equivalent survey-design variance method for the assessed analysis; NOT_USED=explicit design-ignorant variance; NR=variance method unreported; UNC=design components or analysis linkage unclear; NA=no applicable uncertainty analysis. Weights alone do not qualify.
items.legacy.SUR11: [unit: study] (SUR11) Were combined weights used when pooling multiple survey years? Responses: USED; NOT_USED; NR; UNC; NA. USED=explicit survey sampling-weight strategy applied to pooled multiple years, within or across cycles; NOT_USED=explicitly no such strategy applied; NR=pooling established but weighting unreported; UNC (current UNCLEAR)=pooling or application ambiguous, including a described strategy without clear use; NA=single year or years analysed separately with no multi-year pooling. For BOTH, assess the pooled analysis. Class/loss weights do not qualify. Reported strategy (DAT11/12) is not proof of application (DAT13). Do not prescribe an arbitrary year-count formula or infer a defect solely from nonuse; assess relevance to the scientific purpose separately.
items.legacy.PRE05: [unit: study] (PRE05) Was missing-data handling appropriately performed within the train/test or resampling structure? Responses: USED; NOT_USED; NR; UNC; NA.
items.legacy.PRE11: [unit: study] (PRE11) Was supervised feature selection used? Responses: USED; NOT_USED; NR; UNC; NA.
items.legacy.PRE13: [unit: study] (PRE13) Timing of feature selection Responses: WITHIN=Within each resampling training partition; TRAIN=Training data only; BEFORE=Before split; ORDER_NR=Order not reported; NA=No active intervention; OTHER=Other. Selection must be repeated within each training partition.
items.legacy.PRE14: [unit: study] (PRE14) Was all data-driven preprocessing separated from evaluation data? Responses: USED; NOT_USED; NR; UNC; NA.
items.legacy.IMB03: [unit: study] (IMB03) Timing of class-imbalance handling Responses: WITHIN=Within each resampling training partition; TRAIN=Training data only; BEFORE=Before split; ORDER_NR=Order not reported; NA=No active intervention; OTHER=Other.
items.legacy.OUT16: [unit: study] (OUT16) Reproducibility of the outcome definition Responses: R2=Fully recoverable; R1=Partly recoverable; R0=Not recoverable; NA=Not applicable. Apply the R2/R1/R0 rules; record the rationale with evidence.
items.legacy.PRD13: [unit: study] (PRD13) Reconstructability of the predictor set Responses: R2=Fully recoverable; R1=Partly recoverable; R0=Not recoverable; NA=Not applicable. Apply the R2/R1/R0 rules.
items.legacy.MOD15: [unit: study] (MOD15) Code-availability status Responses: PUBLIC_ACCESS_VERIFIED; PUBLIC_LINK_REPORTED_ACCESS_NOT_REVERIFIED; LINK_INACCESSIBLE; AVAILABLE_ON_REQUEST; PARTIAL_CODE_ONLY; NOT_PROVIDED_OR_NOT_REPORTED; UNCLEAR; NA. Distinguish a reported public link, verified access, and failed access.
items.legacy.VAL02: [unit: study] (VAL02) Validation methods Responses: APPARENT=Apparent performance; SPLIT=Single train-test split; CV=Cross-validation; BOOT=Bootstrap; TEMPORAL=Temporal validation; EXTERNAL=External dataset/cycle; NONE_NR=None/not reported; OTHER=Other. Separate multiple codes with semicolons; describe OTHER. Legacy NONE_NR does not distinguish explicit nonuse from absent reporting: retain it as unresolved evaluation status, not confirmed nonuse.
items.legacy.tuning_kept_apart: [unit: study] Was hyperparameter tuning (and model selection) kept apart from the data of the final performance evaluation? USED (tuning on training data or inner resampling only) | NOT_USED (test data used for tuning or selection) | NR | NA (no tuning).
items.legacy.final_model_specified: [unit: study] Is the final model fully specified so that it could be applied (equation with coefficients, tree, score, shared model file or full hyperparameters with code)? R | P | NR.
items.legacy.REP01: [unit: study] (REP01, TRIPOD+AI-derived reporting element) Does the title identify a prediction/model/ML study? Required components: prediction/model/ML identification. Value: R (all required components reported) | P (some) | NR (none); list which components are reported.
